Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details
- Patient: Valerie Cole, DOB: 19/09/1993, Gender: Female, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon
- Referring GP: Doctor Smith, Practice: Babylon, Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Work-related anxiety)
- Secondary: Depressive disorder (moderate, emerging or co-morbid)
- Tertiary: Possible cardiac arrhythmia (to be ruled out)
(DDx supports principal diagnosis of GAD with medium likelihood of depressive disorder and cardiac arrhythmia consistent with transcript)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: None documented
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: No prior psychiatric diagnoses reported; no chronic medical illnesses documented

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: None reported
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): None reported
- Family History: Mother has history of depression

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with retired parents
- Social Support: Good family support; talks regularly with mother
- Occupation/Education: Employed in head office team of a fashion retailer; new to retail sector; reports difficult relationship with boss
- Alcohol Use: Social drinker; increased consumption on Fridays and Saturdays (possibly excessive), occasional glass of wine during week
- Smoking/Substance Use: Occasional smoking, denies drug use
- Key Stressors: New stressful job with a difficult boss, work-related anxiety and fear of underperformance, public transport stress

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Not explicitly described
- Mood & Affect: Distressed, feeling down, low mood reported
- Speech & Thought: No abnormalities noted
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Oriented (implied, no confusion noted)
- Attention/Concentration: No formal testing reported; patient reports difficulty concentrating indirectly via anxiety symptoms
- Memory: Not assessed
- Insight & Judgement: Good insight; recognizes anxiety symptoms and seeks help; worries about worsening symptoms

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Difficulty falling asleep; early morning awakening with palpitations; overall shallow sleep, approximately 3–4 hours per night
- Appetite: No significant change; increased chocolate consumption reported
- Motivation/Energy: Low energy, poor motivation, anhedonia in daily activities and hobbies
- Anxiety Symptoms: Morning nervousness, anticipatory anxiety about work, palpitations described as irregular and sometimes painful, worry about being late, avoidance of social and leisure activities

Risk Assessment:
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: No suicidal ideation or self-harm; denies extreme thoughts; concerned about worsening anxiety but no current acute risk
- Protective Factors: Good family support, motivation to seek help, no substance dependence
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low to moderate
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation:
Valerie’s current anxiety symptoms are primarily precipitated by a new and stressful work environment characterized by a difficult boss and high perceived performance pressure. This has resulted in generalized anxiety symptoms predominantly manifesting as morning nervousness, palpitations, sleep disruption, and subsequent low mood with anhedonia and avoidance of previously enjoyed social activities. Her family history of depression may predispose to mood symptoms. Palpitations and irregular heartbeats raise a possible medical contributor (e.g., arrhythmia or hyperthyroidism), warranting further medical investigation. Low motivation and energy perpetuate symptom chronicity. Protective factors include good familial support and patient motivation for therapy.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Work-related anxiety)
- Patient Goal(s): To reduce anxiety symptoms, improve sleep quality, and regain enjoyment in daily activities
- Clinical Goal(s): To decrease anxiety severity and related functional impairment; prevent deterioration or development of panic attacks
- Actions (Patient): Engage with recommended talking therapy; utilize online self-help resources; monitor symptoms and seek help if worsening
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Refer for NHS talking therapy/self-referral support; provide online resources for anxiety management and sleep hygiene; arrange basic blood tests (thyroid, full blood count, others as indicated) to exclude physical causes of palpitations; organize GP follow-up post-laboratory testing to review results and reassess

Secondary Problem: Depressive disorder (emerging/co-morbid)
- Patient Goal(s): To improve mood, restore motivation and activity levels
- Clinical Goal(s): Early identification and management of depressive symptoms; monitor for deterioration
- Actions (Patient): Attend therapy sessions; maintain social contacts and physical activity as tolerated
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Monitor mood symptoms regularly; consider antidepressant therapy if depressive symptoms worsen or persist post-therapy

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Anxiety symptoms, coping strategies, sleep hygiene, available talking therapies, when to seek urgent care
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increasing avoidance, insomnia worsening, emergence of panic attacks, worsening mood, suicidal ideation
- Coping Strategies: Breathing techniques, accessing online resources, maintaining routine, pacing activity, social support

Consent, Coordination & Review:
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes (implied by participation and acceptance)
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not applicable
- Review Date: One week after blood test results and initiation of therapy referral

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Generalized Anxiety Disorder (Work-related anxiety) — High likelihood; supported by symptom onset linked to stressful job, classic anxiety symptoms with avoidance behavior, and physical symptoms including palpitations and insomnia
- Depressive disorder — Medium likelihood; overlap with anxiety symptoms, presence of low mood, anhedonia, family history of depression
- Cardiac arrhythmia — Medium likelihood; irregular palpitations lasting minutes with chest discomfort warrant cardiology exclusion
- Hyperthyroidism — Medium likelihood; symptoms such as palpitations and anxiety could be explained by thyroid dysfunction but no classic signs present; requires laboratory exclusion
- Substance-related anxiety (alcohol/smoking) — Low likelihood; potential exacerbating factor but not primary cause per clinical history

Quality checks  
● Diagnosis provided consistent with transcript and DDx  
● MSE limited by lack of formal testing and examination details  
● Risk assessment adequately addressed no acute suicidal or self-harm risk  
● Treatment goals and follow-up clearly defined  
● No internal conflicts noted between transcript and DDx  
● Transcript quality good, comprehensive and clear dialogue
